elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New Section 16.7: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — the cap runs against both Array and Ono.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 16.7 caps at "the fees and other amounts payable by Ono ... during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" — no USD 1,000,000 floor and no "paid or payable" formulation (payable only).

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 16.5: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY ... BE LIABLE ... FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES SUFFERED BY THE OTHER PARTY".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 excepts "either Party's breach of Article 10 (Confidentiality)", but retained 16.5 describes "THE INDEMNITIES PROVIDED PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 10", indicating Article 10 may be an indemnity/IP article rather than the Confidentiality article; the caption cannot be confirmed from the supplied text.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 lists only indemnification, Article 10 and gross negligence/willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears anywhere in the rendered language.
16.7: "Except with respect to each Party's indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2 ..."; any Article 10 indemnity is additionally reached by the Article 10 breach carve-out.
16.7 excepts "either Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct".
16.7 excepts "either Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct".
No fraud carve-out appears in 16.7 or elsewhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 contains no carve-out for infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing in 16.7 states that Ono's payment obligations (milestones, royalties, other amounts payable) are not "damages" subject to the cap; on its face the cap could be read to limit recovery of amounts contractually owed.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 16.7 applies "each Party's total aggregate liability" — symmetrical.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 16.7: "the fees and other amounts payable by Ono under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee-based basis.
16.7 opening exception expressly covers "each Party's indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out is drafted by cross-reference only — "breach of Article 10 (Confidentiality)" — while retained 16.5 refers to indemnities "PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 10", so the Article 10 caption is in doubt; if Article 10 is not the confidentiality article the carve-out is a mislabelled cross-reference and the element fails.
16.7: "either Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct" sits outside the cap.
16.7: "either Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct" sits outside the cap.

reasons: Deviation classification is correct on the underlying document: 16.5 is only a mutual consequential-damages waiver; no aggregate monetary or fee-based cap exists, leaving direct liability unlimited for both Parties, which fails the fallback on a material term.
Fallback is all but complete: 16.7 delivers a mutual cap, a 12-month fee basis, and express carve-outs for indemnification under 16.1/16.2 and for gross negligence/willful misconduct.

Blocking defect: the confidentiality carve-out is expressed solely as "breach of Article 10 (Confidentiality)", but retained 16.5 speaks of "THE INDEMNITIES PROVIDED PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 10", which indicates Article 10 may be an indemnity/IP article, not Confidentiality. Repair by confirming the Article caption and, safest, drafting the carve-out functionally: "either Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations (Article [X])" so the element does not depend on a possibly wrong cross-reference and does not contradict 16.5.

Recommended secondary repair (not required at fallback): 16.5 carves indemnities under Article 10 as well as 16.1/16.2 out of the damages waiver, whereas 16.7 names only 16.1 and 16.2; align the two lists so Article 10 indemnities are indisputably outside the cap.

Preferred level remains unmet (no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, "payable" rather than "paid or payable", no data protection/security, fraud or other-party IP carve-outs, and no statement that Ono's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap) — acceptable if fallback is the chosen target, but the confidentiality reference must be fixed first.

Minimality holds: a single concise new section is inserted, 16.5 is left untouched, and no survival tails, expense language or extra procedures are added; "fees and other amounts payable by Ono" is a reasonable adaptation because this pharma licence pays milestones and royalties rather than "fees".
Intent is otherwise preserved: the recall/regulatory paragraph and the mutual consequential-damages waiver survive without contradiction, subject to confirming the Article 10 caption.
